saints.name: St. Augustine of Canterbury
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: The Roman monk sent by Pope Gregory the Great to convert the English, and first Archbishop of Canterbury…
biography: Prior of St. Andrew's monastery on the Caelian Hill in Rome, Augustine was chosen by Pope Gregory the Great in 595 to lead a band of monks to the English. They landed on the Isle of Thanet in Kent in 597 and were received by King Ethelbert, whose Frankish wife Bertha was already a Christian.

Ethelbert was baptized, and at Christmas in 597 thousands of his people followed him. Consecrated bishop at Arles, Augustine fixed his see at Canterbury, built the cathedral of Christ Church, and founded outside the walls the monastery of Sts. Peter and Paul, later called St. Augustine's Abbey. Reinforcements sent by Gregory in 601 let him set up further sees at London and Rochester in 604.

His attempts to bring the old British Christians into Roman observance failed, but the see he planted endured. He died about the year 604 and was buried in the monastery he had founded. As the first Archbishop of Canterbury and leader of Gregory's mission, he is venerated as the Apostle of the English and a patron of England.
saints.knownFor: The conversion of the English and the founding of the see of Canterbury.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 26 May
